 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Paulson Adebo is back on the Giants' active roster. The club activated the cornerback Saturday , adding an option before Houston after a knee issue had kept him on injured reserve.
 I'd give him a defined assignment before expecting him to carry a full afternoon. The Giants need help at corner, but being eligible to play and being prepared to handle every defensive snap are separate questions.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The size of the gap is worth remembering. Adebo appeared in one game this season, against Dallas in Week 1. He played 10 defensive snaps and eight on special teams before going on injured reserve. He hasn't had a normal starter's accumulation of game work in this defense.
 2026 summer practice archive, not his October return to game action. New York Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo (21) looks on while at Quest Diagnostics Training Center, Aug 10, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect
 The Giants are getting an option back, with others still missing
 Greg Newsome II remains out with a concussion, and the Giants also ruled Jevon Holland out Saturday. Adebo's activation arrives while the secondary is losing other experienced players, rather than returning to full strength around him.
 That puts some responsibility on the deployment plan. I'd want the coaches to establish which coverage jobs Adebo can handle confidently and keep the other corners involved. Rotating him by series is one possible approach, not a restriction the Giants have announced.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 0What do you think? Post a comment. 
 There is a reasonable argument for giving him more work if his preparation supports it. Adebo played 12 games for New York in 2025, and holding back an effective corner simply to satisfy an arbitrary snap target would make little sense. The staff has information from practice and his medical evaluation that isn't available outside the building.
 Activation doesn't decide the workload
 The new transaction is important because the earlier opening of his practice window did not guarantee a return for Houston. The Giants have now taken the next step. They haven't publicly attached a snap count or promised a starting assignment to it.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Adebo should have the chance to earn more work through the way he plays, with enough room in the plan to adjust if the long layoff shows. A specific coverage assignment is a fair first task; the other absences still have to be managed by the rest of the defense.
